Hi John + Jane — thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, below is a short recap of how Redwood handles prompts and outputs (high level) and the immediate next steps we agreed on. Let me know if I missed anything.

Recap (high level):
- Hosted API (standard): we capture request & response text and related metadata for operational/debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring by default. Retention is 30 days by default, configurable via contract for enterprise customers. Data is stored in the region you select (US or EU) for regional residency requirements.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): logs/telemetry can be limited. We offer options to disable storing full prompt/output text and only retain very small operational metadata or forward logs to your logging endpoint. Dedicated customers can contract custom retention and redaction rules.
- Private / On-prem: you control where data lives. By default, data does not leave your VPC (or on-prem environment).
- Training use: we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models unless explicitly opted in under a separate agreement.
- Encryption & access: all data is encrypted at rest and in transit; role-based access and audit logs are available. KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments.

Open items / next steps:
1) Neha (cc'd) will send the security one-pager and confirm retention/region language we can include in the SOW.
2) John/Jane to confirm whether you need output prompt redaction (PII removal) or full redact/disable logging for the pilot.
3) We'll produce a short SOW addendum that outlines retention, residency, encryption, and logging controls for Dedicated/Private options.

Attachments: redwood-pii-summary.pdf (one-pager) & acme-mdap-questionnaire.xlsx (your filled questionnaire — thanks!).

Thanks — I'll follow up once Neha sends the security summary.

Hi John (& Jane),

Thanks for the concrete questions — below are the specifics to help your security and infra teams. I'm attaching a one-pager (pii-handling-one-pager.pdf) that summarizes these points for the SOW.

Detailed answers: 
- Inference/runtime caching: during request processing we use in-memory KV caches to store model past keys for performance. These caches are ephemeral and are not persisted to durable storage by default. For Dedicated, there may be short-lived cache copies on the serving host (memory + GPU buffers) but we do not persist prompt/output text to disk unless logging is explicitly enabled.
- Logging/retention: Hosted API logs (which include request text and generated output by default) are kept for 30 days for abuse monitoring, debugging, and to support incident investigations. For enterprise customers we can: (a) set retention to a lower configurable window, (b) redact PII fields at ingest, or (c) disable storing full prompt/output text entirely — in the latter case, we retain minimal operational metadata (timestamps, request size, model variant, latency, error codes) for SLA and billing reconciliation.
- 0-day retention (no text stored): choosing 0-day/full disable means we will not retain the prompt/output text in our logs after the ephemeral processing window. You will lose some debugability for production incidents (no replay of exact request/response), and certain abuse detection features that rely on historical text will be limited; we recommend a short buffer (e.g., 1–7 days) during early pilot to surface any issues.
- Training/data usage: we do not use customer-provided prompts/outputs to train models unless you opt in under a separate agreement; this is documented in our DPA and Data Processing Addendum.
- Data residency: Hosted logs are stored in the region you select (US or EU). Dedicated customers can have logging routed to a customer-managed logging endpoint (e.g., your Splunk/Datadog or S3) to ensure residency controls. Private/on-prem keeps logs entirely inside your network.
- Encryption & access controls: logs and stored artefacts are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). We offer integration with customer-managed KMS for key control in Dedicated/Private setups. All internal access is role-based with field-level redaction available and audit logging for any data access.

Next steps we can take this week:
- I'll produce short language snippets for SOW (retention, redaction options, region clause) that Marissa can include.
- If you want to test redaction, we can run a PoC where we redact PII at ingest and forward anonymized logs to your Splunk for a week.

Attaching: pii-handling-one-pager.pdf (summary), redwood-pii-summary.pdf (detailed), acme-mdap-questionnaire.xlsx (your submitted questionnaire — retained for reference).
